narratives.Description: bug(review-cycle): a repository with no reviewer installed cannot reach a terminal state — absence reads as "review pending"
narratives.Overview:
1. Before entering the review-cycle / pr:watch poll loop, determine once whether a reviewer can be expected (presence probe and/or explicit policy). If none can, exit immediately with a named non-CLEAN terminal (e.g. not-configured / no-reviewer-installed) that is distinguishable from clean, blocked, TIMEOUT, and dual-stop stall.
2. That terminal must be inherited by task pr:watch and pr:merge-ready so none of them can hang on a reviewer-less repository. Reuse the existing "named weather terminal, not CLEAN" pattern from CI_NEVER_SCHEDULED / related CI gates (#3167 / #2672). Extend the shared probe/watch SoT; do not invent a second detector or a third poller.
3. Keep the fail-closed rule that empty observation must never CLEAN. A configured-but-slow reviewer must still poll (absent/slow distinction tested both ways). Ambiguity between slow and absent stays fail-closed to poll or to an explicit operator/policy declaration — not to CLEAN.
4. Zero-reviewer exit routes to deft-directive-pre-pr self-review rather than skipping review entirely, with a canonical handback value (e.g. review_cycle: skipped:no-reviewer-installed) so parents can tell "no reviewer" apart from "reviewer said nothing."
5. Orientation: doctor and/or review-cycle preflight reports reviewer presence. Preflight must not only check Greptile settings that presuppose an installed app.
6. #769 stays the substitution / multi-profile grain. Empty registry / zero-reviewer is a named requirement on #3630 (or an explicit #769 acceptance limb that empty registry is terminal and routes to self-review). Do not bind "#769 alone covers permanent absence."
7. Tests + CHANGELOG: fixture with no reviewer exits in one pass without polling; fixture with slow reviewer still polls; pr:watch / pr:merge-ready inherit the determination.

issueCommentThread.body:
Adoption blocker.

This is about Gates: the check that stands in the doorway before work is called good. A green result should mean Directive actually looked. A red result should say what to do next.

What a new person hits: If the repository has no review bot installed, the pull request never reaches a finished state. Missing a reviewer looks like "still waiting."

Why that ruins the product for them: The first pull request sits forever. They think they are waiting on a person. They are waiting on a tool that is not there.

How likely: Medium-high for a personal project, which will not have a review bot. That is the typical first repository.

model: grok-4.5
```quarantined
role: triage
```

mechanism-shaped: true
design-critique: warranted, because review-cycle / pr:watch treat permanent reviewer absence the same as "review pending": Step 6 fail-closed all-of resolves every missing field to unknown and returns to the poll, so a repository with no bot reviewer installed can only exit by dual-stop budget exhaustion reported as a stall.

charter: refutation
refutation-target: On a repository with no reviewer bot installed, it is acceptable that review-cycle and pr:watch keep treating permanent absence as "review pending" / unknown and poll until dual-stop budget exhaustion, because the fail-closed all-of and late-arriving re-check correctly prefer "pending" over "clean" and #769's profile registry alone will eventually cover it.

arc-mode: no-ingest
yolo-standing: yes
spend: N=1
spend-ask: asked

The operator continued the evaluate/label/arc campaign and previously authorized pick recommended N. This is a concrete wait-verb / zero-reviewer terminal defect (absence vs slowness), not a whole-motion open design panel. Recommended spend N=1. Adjacent to #769 (wrong-reviewer substitution) but the zero-reviewer case needs its own terminal.

pain: P1, P2, P3

P1. With no reviewer installed, Step 6's fail-closed all-of is unsatisfiable by construction; the agent polls until dual-stop budget and reports a stall, not a diagnosis (measured ~55 min on one run).
P2. Absence and slowness are the same observation today (late-arriving re-check prefers "pending"); there is no preflight / ReviewerStatus / doctor / policy path that can terminate "not configured" before the loop.
P3. Consumers work around with per-PR out-of-band "ignore Greptile" instructions; the zero case must be a named terminal that routes to pre-pr self-review and is inherited by pr:watch / pr:merge-ready without GraphQL gh pr view --json. #769 profile registry alone does not resolve empty-registry as terminal.

## Verdict on the refutation target

The refutation target does **not** survive. Preferring "pending" over "clean" on a missing review is the right fail-closed rule for a configured-but-slow bot; treating permanent zero-reviewer absence as that same pending state until dual-stop / max-wait exhaustion is a distinct, diagnosable hang that #769's substitution registry does not close.

## Absence shares the sha_match keep-polling path to TIMEOUT
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At the dispatch SHA, `evaluateCleanGate` (`packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts`) returns holdout `sha_match` when `lastReviewedSha` is null. `fetchGreptileCommentBody` jq uses `.body // ""`, so no Greptile comment yields an empty body (`found: false`), not a probe error. `watch()` (`packages/core/src/pr-watch/watch.ts`) advances the STALL streak only when `cleanGateHoldout !== "sha_match"`; the locked test `"TIMEOUT when the review never appears before the cap"` drives `found: false` + `cleanGateHoldout: "sha_match"` to `VERDICT_TIMEOUT`, and `"does NOT STALL on stale-SHA confidence during re-review (#2313)"` keeps the same holdout on the poll-to-cap path. Skill Step 6 fail-closed all-of plus the late-arriving re-check (`content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md`) resolve the same empty observation to `unknown` / "review pending" and return to the loop.
Failure mode: On a repo with no reviewer installed, `pr:watch` / review-cycle / drive-to:merge-ready merge-path waits burn the dual-stop or `--max-wait-minutes` budget and hand back TIMEOUT/STALL-shaped exhaustion. The operator learns the agent gave up, not that the repository has no reviewer; shared merge-path wait authority stays occupied for the full cap on a permanent condition.
Disposition: Before bind, reject "acceptable to keep treating absence as pending until budget exhaustion." Require a named zero-reviewer / not-configured determination that terminates before the poll loop, while keeping the fail-closed rule that empty observation must never CLEAN.

## #769 profile registry does not terminate the empty set
blocks-the-design
Evidence: Live REST body of open #769 (fetched this seat) scopes three scenarios: Slizard alongside Greptile, Slizard instead of Greptile, and future reviewers. The proposed registry entries assume a profile with comment markers, exit conditions, and expected duration. The substitution failure mode named there is "no Greptile review found -> wait forever" when another bot is configured. Stop 1 P3 already records that an empty registry is a different case; nothing in #769's body names empty-registry / zero-profile as a legitimate terminal configuration or a self-review handback.
Failure mode: Binding " #769 alone will eventually cover it" lets a shipped multi-profile registry still leave personal/consumer repos with no bot installed on the same keep-polling path, because there is no profile to select and no empty-set terminal in that design.
Disposition: Treat zero-reviewer as a named requirement on this issue (or an explicit #769 acceptance limb that empty registry is terminal and routes to pre-pr self-review). Do not bind the target's claim that the profile registry alone covers permanent absence.

## Sibling CI weather already names permanent absence; reviewer axis does not
sharpens-framing
Evidence: `packages/core/src/pr-watch/constants.ts` and `watch.ts` already exit 2 on `CI_NEVER_SCHEDULED` / `RUNNER_CAPACITY_STALL` / `CI_CANCELLED_NO_FAILOVER` so agents thrash-cap rather than multi-hour empty loops (#3167 / #2672). No analogous reviewer-side verdict exists for "no bot will ever post." `plan.policy.review` at this SHA only exposes `minGreptileConfidence` (a floor for a score that never arrives). Greptile preflight checks `triggerOnUpdates` / `statusCheck` / `@greptileai` re-trigger — all presuppose an installed app. Doctor under `packages/core/src/doctor/` has no reviewer-presence line (grep at dest: Greptile mentions are pin/display accuracy, not bot install).
Failure mode: If the bound remedy only softens skill prose without a shared terminal inherited by `pr:watch` / `pr:merge-ready`, CI-shaped permanent hangs stay diagnosable while reviewer-shaped permanent hangs keep burning merge-path wait authority.
Disposition: When stating the Bound remedy, reuse the existing "named weather terminal, not CLEAN" pattern from CI gates; require inheritance by the shared wait verbs; orientation (doctor or preflight presence probe) is supporting, not a substitute for the wait terminal.

## Injection / swarm lens
Shared merge-path wait authority (`pr:watch`, review-cycle Step 6, Approach 1 / Phase 6 monitors, drive-to:merge-ready leaves) is exactly the surface this target changes. A false-positive "not configured" that CLEANs would merge un-reviewed code — that remains forbidden. The needed control is a distinct non-CLEAN terminal (plus handback that routes to `deft-directive-pre-pr` self-review), fail-closed on any ambiguity between slow and absent, with the slow path still polling. Do not invent a second detector; extend the existing probe/watch SoT so orchestrators cannot promise a wait that silently evaporates into budget exhaustion without a diagnosis.

## Road not taken
Steelmanning the target: empty observation must not CLEAN (#1259), late-arriving re-check is correct for cold-start, dual-stop eventually stops the burn, and #769 could grow a "none" profile later. What flips that: the locked `found: false` → `sha_match` → TIMEOUT path proves absence is deliberately kept on the in-flight poll path; dual-stop/TIMEOUT handbacks do not diagnose install; #769's live body never names empty registry as terminal; consumer first-PR cost (~55 min in the issue body) is the expected personal-repo case, not a rare edge.

## Existing mechanisms inventoried (no new invention required to see the gap)
- Step 6 fail-closed all-of + late-arriving re-check (skill)
- `probeOnce` / `watch` / `evaluateCleanGate` / verdict constants (pr-watch)
- `minGreptileConfidence` only under `plan.policy.review`
- #1543 informal-clean (bot comment present, canonical fields missing — different grain)
- Stall menu "skip bot review" (operator pick after stall — not a pre-loop presence terminal)
- #769 open profile-registry proposal (substitution, not zero)
- Doctor: no reviewer presence check at this SHA

## In plain English

On a repo with no reviewer bot installed, review-cycle and pr:watch treat permanent absence as "review pending" and poll until dual-stop / TIMEOUT, so the handback is budget exhaustion rather than a diagnosis. Preferring pending over clean for a slow bot is right; using that same path for permanent zero-reviewer is not. #769's profile registry covers substitution, not empty registry. Confirming this map means the Bound remedy list is the build contract. The same parent wrote the Stop 1 warrant and this map. Critic 5857889140 checks the findings. Whether the list covers the three pains stays open until a later critic targets those cites.

**Lean:** the refutation target does not survive. This map is the bind.

## Summary

`deft-directive-review-cycle` has no terminal state for "this repository has no bot reviewer installed". Step 6's fail-closed all-of resolves every missing field to `unknown`, and `unknown` sends the agent back to Step 2. On a repository where no reviewer will ever post, all five fields are permanently absent, so the predicate is unsatisfiable by construction and the loop can only end by exhausting its dual-stop budget (#2442) — reported as a stall, not as a diagnosis.

The operator-visible symptom is that a PR "just sits there". The workaround that consumers land on is to tell every agent, on every PR, by hand: *Greptile is not installed, ignore it.* If they forget, the agent waits.

This is adjacent to #769 but not covered by it — see **Relationship to #769** below.

## Reproduction

1. A repository with no reviewer bot installed — no Greptile app, no `.greptile/config.json`, no `Greptile Review` check run, no reviewer comments. (Verified across four PRs on the consumer repo below.)
2. Open a PR and route it through `deft-directive-review-cycle`, or hand it to a swarm worker scoped `drive-to: merge-ready`.
3. The agent enters the Step 4 polling loop and never leaves it.

Observed cost on one run: a worker agent spent **55 minutes** in `deft pr:watch` before concluding the bot was absent, and it only stopped because of the dual-stop no-progress envelope. Nothing in that 55 minutes was recoverable work.

## Implementation evidence

**The exit predicate cannot be satisfied without a reviewer.** `skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` § Step 6:

> The loop MAY exit clean ONLY when a SINGLE fresh fetch … satisfies ALL of the `ReviewerStatus` fields below. This is a **fail-closed all-of**: any field that is missing, unparsed, or ambiguous resolves to **`unknown`**, and `unknown` is NOT a pass — the agent stays in the loop and returns to Step 2.

All five fields — terminal `Greptile Review` check run, HEAD-pinned reviewed SHA, `Last reviewed commit` marker, parsed `Confidence Score: X/5`, P0/P1 detector — are properties of a reviewer comment or check run that will never exist. This is correct and desirable when a reviewer is configured; it has no escape when one is not.

**The one rule that could break the tie decides the wrong way.** Same file:

> **Late-arriving bot review re-check:** If the initial dual-source fetch returns no bot review on the current HEAD SHA, wait ~60s and re-fetch … an empty first pass is more likely "review pending" than "review clean".

That heuristic is right for a slow reviewer and exactly wrong for an absent one, and the skill has no way to tell the two apart. Absence and slowness are the same observation.

**The preflight checks the reviewer's settings, never its presence.** § "Before entering the review/fix loop, verify the Greptile configuration supports it" checks `triggerOnUpdates`, `statusCheck`, and the `@greptileai` re-trigger fallback. Every item presupposes an installed app. There is no step that asks whether a reviewer exists at all, and no `ReviewerStatus` value that could carry the answer.

**Nothing else terminates it.** `plan.policy.review.minGreptileConfidence` (#3095) resolves a floor for a score that will never be parsed. `task pr:watch` / `pr:merge-ready` share that SoT and inherit the same unsatisfiable predicate. The dual-stop rule (#2442) does eventually halt the agent, but it reports budget exhaustion — an operator reading that handback learns the agent gave up, not that the repository has no reviewer.

## Relationship to #769

#769 (open since 2026-04-30) proposes named reviewer profiles and explicitly lists the failure mode:

> **Slizard instead of Greptile** — on PRs where only Slizard is configured, Greptile-specific gates produce false negatives ("no Greptile review found -> wait forever").

That is the *substitution* case: a reviewer exists, but it is the wrong one, and the fix is a profile registry. The **zero-reviewer** case is different in three ways that a profile registry does not resolve on its own:

1. There is no profile to select. An empty registry has to be a legitimate, terminal configuration — not an unmatched lookup.
2. The correct outcome is not "parse a different comment shape" but "stop, and substitute a self-review". That is a different exit, with a different handback value.
3. It affects consumers who never intended to install a reviewer, which is likely to be most consumers outside the framework's own repository. #769 is scoped to the framework's own multi-reviewer needs.

A profile registry is a natural home for the fix, but the zero case needs to be a named requirement or it will be designed around.

## Actual behavior

An agent on a reviewer-less repository polls until its budget is exhausted, then reports a stall. The operator must pre-empt this on every PR with an out-of-band instruction. No `deft` verb, policy field, or doctor check reports that the repository has no reviewer.

## Expected behavior

The skill determines once, before entering the loop, whether a reviewer can be expected. If none can, it exits immediately with a distinct, non-failure terminal state, records that in the handback, and directs the agent to the `deft-directive-pre-pr` self-review instead of a poll.

## Possible mechanisms (not a decided design)

- **A presence probe in the existing preflight.** The check the preflight already performs — `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` — answers most of it. Combined with "no reviewer comment on any of the last N merged PRs", it distinguishes "not installed" from "slow" without waiting.
- **A sixth `ReviewerStatus` value: `not-configured`.** Terminal, distinct from `unknown`, and distinct from `clean` — it asserts nothing about the code, only about the repository.
- **A typed policy field**, e.g. `plan.policy.review.reviewers: []`, letting an operator declare the answer instead of it being probed. An empty list is a valid, explicit configuration. This also gives #769's registry its zero case for free.
- **A `doctor` line.** "Reviewer: none detected" alongside the existing hook and toolchain lines would surface it at orientation rather than at minute 55.
- **A named handback value.** `review_cycle: skipped:no-reviewer-installed` is what one consumer settled on by hand; making it canonical means a parent agent can tell "no reviewer" apart from "reviewer said nothing".

## Acceptance criteria

- A fixture repository with no reviewer installed exits `deft-directive-review-cycle` in one pass, without polling.
- The exit is terminal and distinguishable from both `clean` and `blocked` in the handback.
- A fixture with a reviewer that is merely slow still polls — the absent/slow distinction is tested in both directions.
- `task pr:watch` and `pr:merge-ready` inherit the same determination; none of them can hang on a reviewer-less repository.
- The zero-reviewer case is reachable without an operator instruction on each PR.
- Orientation (`doctor`, or the review-cycle preflight) reports reviewer presence.
- A reviewer-less exit routes to the `deft-directive-pre-pr` self-review rather than skipping review entirely.
- CHANGELOG.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` 0.106.0, engine and content 0.106.0
- consumer deposit, hybrid mode; GitHub forge; no reviewer app installed on the repository
- verified absent across four PRs on the consumer repo (no check-run, no review, no comment)
- Claude Code host, Windows 11
